extracted.intended_audience: attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; disciplinary counsel and regulators
extracted.subtask_description: A final order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state-court suspension; describes procedure, grounds for discipline, specific misconduct findings, sanctions, and notice/publication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for imposing reciprocal discipline when a practitioner is disciplined by a state court: the Deputy General Counsel files a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and the Director may impose discipline identical to the state order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a response may lead to a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and to imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for USPTO discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline may be imposed pursuant to USPTO ethical rules where a practitioner has been disciplined by a state court for violations of rules of professional conduct that correspond to USPTO standards (here cited as 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the respondent "violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) when he was disciplined by the Supreme Court of Minnesota" and uses the state-court findings as the predicate for USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The discipline was predicated upon a determination that the respondent violated Minnesota Rules of Professional Conduct (including Rule 1.3) by "neglecting multiple client matters."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect of client matters is treated as a professional misconduct basis for suspension; the state-court determination of neglect is accepted in the USPTO reciprocal proceeding absent a successful challenge under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing documents without client consent
rubrics_metrics.description: State-court findings included that the respondent signed documents without client consent, identified as a violation of the Minnesota Rules of Professional Conduct and Rule 25 of the Rules on Lawyers Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized signing of documents with respect to client matters is cited as misconduct supporting discipline before the USPTO when established by the disciplining authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to return client files
rubrics_metrics.description: The state court found the respondent failed to return client files, a violation cited among the grounds for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to return client files upon request or termination of representation is treated as serious misconduct and cited as a basis for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to cooperate with disciplinary investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent was found to have failed to cooperate with the disciplinary investigation, and that failure was cited as a basis for the state suspension and the USPTO's reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncooperation with disciplinary authorities is a separate ground for discipline and may support suspension in reciprocal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions imposed: suspension and limits on reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order imposes suspension from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office for a minimum of 120 days and sets conditions on reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After serving the 120-day suspension, the respondent "may request reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 for the sole purpose of being placed on voluntary inactive status consistent with 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(d)." The respondent "shall not apply for reinstatement to actively practice before the USPTO" and "shall not be permitted to be restored to active status on the register after serving the 120 day suspension."

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 / Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states of admission, courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided). The Final Order instructs OED to provide notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to relevant agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory provisions including 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these authorities as the legal basis for imposing reciprocal discipline and for publication/notice obligations; practitioners and OED actions are governed by those statutes and regulations.
